title: Shower and Laundry Specialist (S&L SPC)
raw_text:
10-92S. MOS 92S-Shower and Laundry Specialist (S&L SPC), CMF 92 (RC Only) (Eff 202510)
  a. Major duties. The Shower/Laundry Specialist is responsible for operating and maintaining shower
and laundry facilities, including hospital laundry systems, to provide essential hygiene services and
support unit morale by performing laundry services. Duties for MOS 92S at each level of skill are:
     (1) MOSC 92S1O. Operate and maintain basic laundry and shower equipment, following established
procedures. Receive, sort, and wash laundry, ensuring proper cleaning and sanitation. Distribute clean
laundry to designated personnel. Prepare and maintain shower facilities, ensuring cleanliness and
hygiene. Assist with inventory management of laundry supplies and chemicals. Follow safety protocols
when handling chemicals and operating equipment.
     (2) MOSC 92S2O. Supervise preventative maintenance checks and services on laundry and shower
equipment. Troubleshoot minor equipment malfunctions, performing basic repairs. Supervise laundry and
shower operations, ensure quality control and efficiency. Manage laundry and supply inventories, order
replacements as needed. Maintain records of laundry and shower usage, reporting discrepancies.
     (3) MOSC 92S3O. Supervise and train personnel in laundry and shower operations, enforcing
standards. Supervise operator maintenance and repairs on laundry and shower systems. Analyze
equipment performance, identifying and resolving operational issues. Manage the flow of laundry and
supplies, optimizing efficiency and minimizing waste. Inspect facilities for sanitation and hygiene,
implementing corrective actions.
     (4) MOSC 92S4O. Manage all aspects of shower and laundry facilities, including personnel,
equipment, and resources. Develop and implement operational plans, ensuring effective support for units.
Oversee quality control programs, maintaining compliance with health and sanitation standards.
Coordinate with other units to provide laundry and shower services during deployments and exercises.
Analyze data and prepare reports on facility operations and resource utilization.
     (5) MOSC 92S5O. Develop and implement comprehensive laundry and shower support plans at
theater or major command level. Advise commanders on logistical requirements and resource allocation
for laundry and hygiene services. Evaluate and improve operational procedures, incorporating best
practices and new technologies. Manage large-scale laundry and shower operations, overseeing multiple
facilities and personnel. Conduct inspections and audits to ensure compliance with regulations and
standards. Research and recommend solutions for complex laundry and hygiene challenges.
  b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Shower and laundry specialists
must possess the following qualifications:
     (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
     (2) A physical profile of 222222.
     (3) Per AR 600-8-19, promotion to MSG and SGM requires an interim secret eligibility or higher.
     (4) Qualifying scores.
         (a) A minimum score of 84 in aptitude area GM.
         (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0140 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) –
0400 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0040 shuttles in Physical
Demand Category in “Significant” (Gray).
     (5) Formal training. Completion of MOS 92S course conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army
Quartermaster School. Waiver requests can be submitted to the Office of the Quartermaster
Commandant Enlisted Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee, VA, 23801. TRADOC List QM Enlisted
Personnel Development usarmy.lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
  c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS)).
          (1) D6--Operational Data analyst (personnel only)
  d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92S-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92S-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-92S-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
